artifacts.notes:
WHAT THIS IS: uncorrected optical character recognition of an Ambrosian Missal of
1712 together with Masses printed at Milan in 1733 and bound in with it, 77,003
LF-terminated lines, valid UTF-8, no CR bytes, no form feeds, no NUL bytes,
ending in a newline. Registered as a source artifact and nothing more;
deliberately NOT structured as liturgical records. THERE ARE NO PAGE BOUNDARIES
IN THIS FILE, which matters twice here: a line range over it is not a printed-page
range, and it cannot on its own separate the 1712 stratum from the 1733 one. The
item's per-leaf recognition (`10869665bsb_djvu.xml`, 625 `<OBJECT>` elements) can,
and was used for exactly that here.

THE OCR ENGINE WAS RUN ON THE WRONG LANGUAGE AND THE FILE IS STILL THE BEST OF
THE THREE AMBROSIAN LAYERS. The item records `ocr = tesseract 5.3.0-6-g76ae` with
`ocr_parameters = -l eng` -- ENGLISH -- and `ocr-additional-languages = Fraktur`,
on a book that is entirely Latin. The commissioning brief predicted the text layer
would therefore be poor. IT WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE CAUSE AND WRONG ABOUT THE
CONSEQUENCE, and the measurement is recorded rather than the prediction:
scripts/_ocr_quality.py gives a Latin function-word share of 0.1259 over 255,294
tokens, English 0.0323, classified `prose-latin` -- the highest Latin share of the
three Ambrosian files and above the 0.1086 of the 1640, which had ABBYY and the
right language. The item's own metadata agrees the language was detected
correctly even though the recognition was not configured for it:
`ocr_detected_lang = la` at confidence 1.0000 and `ocr_detected_script = Latin` at
0.9972. The English model shows up as scattered word-shaped nonsense
(`Sie a sll hs Bl hs hn`) on ornamental and display pages rather than as damage
across the running text, and it is worst exactly where there is least to lose.
Note also `ppi = 72`, the lowest of this acquisition.

The remaining damage is the ordinary two-column interleave: the book sets two
columns to the page and consecutive lines frequently belong to different columns.
Read a locus, do not read a run. A HEADING SPLIT ACROSS THE COLUMN BREAK IS
INVISIBLE TO A LINE-BY-LINE SEARCH -- this is the file that proved it. The first
anachronism sweep of this lane ran line by line and reported St Aloysius Gonzaga
and St John Nepomucene ABSENT from this book. Both are in it, at leaves n602 and
n604, and both are canonized after the Missal's imprint. They were found only
when the sweep was rebuilt to probe whole leaves. Every negative reported for
this acquisition was re-run at leaf level for that reason.

WHAT THE FILE CONTAINS AND WHERE, READ RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The letterpress title
page is at leaf n10, lines 308-326: `NOVISSIME / CARDINALIS ARCHINTI /
ARCHIEPISCOPI / Auctoritate recognitum / MEDIOLANI, MDCCXIj. / Apud Beniamin, &
Fratres de Sirturis, Impressores Archiepiscopales. / CUM PRIVILEGIO.` The
archbishop's letter follows. The alphabetical index of saints is at n13 to n11
(lines 470, 739). The kalendar runs from about line 730 to about line 1500 with
the Milanese sanctoral in it -- `S. Martiniani Episc. Mediolani`, `S. Benigni
Episc. Mediolani`, `S. Castritiani Episc. Mediolani`, `S. Caroli Episc. Mediol.
4 Novembris`, and NONE of the four 1733 saints. The rubrics and ceremonial run
from about line 3100. The body of the Missal occupies the bulk of the file. The
pontifical and baptismal matter that is the archbishop's own office runs from
about line 70790. THE 1733 FASCICLES BEGIN AFTER ALL OF THAT, at leaf n596: the
Mass of the Most Holy Name of Jesus (n596-598), a terminal colophon `MEDIOLANI,
MDCCXXXIII` at n598 (line 75817), the Mass of St Francis de Sales (n600-601), St
Aloysius Gonzaga (n602), St John Nepomucene (n604-605), and the Mass of St
Raphael printed twice with its own 1733 title page each time (n606-608 and
n612-614). The last leaf, n624, is the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek's digitisation
card.

IDENTITY AND EXTENT. Internet Archive item `10869665bsb`, 625 leaves,
`imagecount = 625`, matching the 625 `<OBJECT>` elements of the item's own
djvu.xml counted here. Uploaded 2026-05-24. The copy is Munich, Bayerische
Staatsbibliothek, Res/2 Liturg. 182. The item's `language` field says `English`,
which is simply wrong and is recorded so that a later reader searching by
language does not conclude the book is not there. The companion page-image
container is the item's `10869665bsb.pdf`, 1,073,348,269 bytes, which is not
registered: at 1.07 GB it is far beyond what this repository has cause to hold,
and the one reading taken from the images here -- the 1733 title page at n606 --
was taken from the item's per-leaf derivative.

WHAT A READER MUST DO BEFORE READING ANY LITURGY OUT OF THIS BOOK. Two things,
in order. First, `read_from = "not-read"` on the Ambrosian witness rows in
src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml is still correct and was not
touched by the lane that wrote this record; nothing in this repository has read a
unit of the Ambrosian use. Second, and specific to this file: ESTABLISH WHICH
STRATUM A PASSAGE COMES FROM BEFORE ATTRIBUTING IT TO 1712. Nothing turns on it
for rights, but a formulary quoted off leaf n602 as evidence of the Ambrosian use
in 1712 would be twenty-one years wrong, and the leaf boundary that settles it is
not in this file.
artifacts.rights_basis:
Public domain in the United States because every stratum of this volume was first
published outside the United States before the pre-1931 line, and on that ground
alone. THE PHRASE `EVERY STRATUM` IS DOING WORK HERE AND IS NOT DECORATIVE: THIS
FILE IS NOT A SINGLE PRINTING.

THE LINE, AND THE YEAR IT WAS DERIVED FOR. Any work first published abroad before
1931 is out of United States copyright; that is the line guidance/missals.md
records from Cornell's public-domain chart as current on 1 January 2026. THE LINE
MOVES EVERY JANUARY -- guidance/missals.md:249 states it in terms -- so it is
written here as DERIVED FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2026 and not as a standing rule: on
1 January 2027 it becomes before 1932. The Missal was published in 1712 and the
latest matter bound into the copy scanned was published in 1733, so the file
clears the 2026 line at its youngest point by a hundred and ninety-eight years.
URAA restoration reaches neither: a restored term runs at most 95 years from
publication, expiring in 1807 for the Missal and 1828 for the added Masses.

THE DATE TEST FOUND SOMETHING, AND IT IS WHY THIS BASIS IS WORDED AS IT IS. The
brief for this lane required the printed date to be tested against the book's own
pages, because two acquisitions had already been refused for failing that test:
the 1920 Missale Romanum, whose appendix printed a Mass granted to a society
erected in 1970, and the Braga scan, which proved to be a 1924 book plus fifteen
supplement leaves running to 1961. THE SAME KIND OF THING IS TRUE OF THIS FILE
AND THE RIGHTS CONSEQUENCE IS THE OPPOSITE. Bound at the end of the scanned
volume, after the Missal's own last quire, are Masses printed at Milan in 1733 by
order of Cardinal Odescalchi, two of which print saints canonized after 1712:

  leaf n602  ST ALOYSIUS GONZAGA, `SANCTI ALOYSII GONZAGAE CONFESSORIS DIE XXVI.
             APRILIS` -- canonized 31 December 1726, fourteen years after the
             Missal's imprint;
  leaf n604  ST JOHN NEPOMUCENE, `SANCTI IOANNIS NEPOMUCENI SACERD. ET MARTYR.`
             -- canonized 19 March 1729, seventeen years after it.

Their date is printed on their own title pages and was read in the page image:
leaf n606 reads `MISSA SANCTI RAPHAELIS ARCHANGELI ... JUSSU Eminentiss. &
Reverendiss. D. D. BENEDICTI ... Card. ODESCALCHI Sanctae Mediolanensis Ecclesiae
Archiepiscopi. NOVISSIME IMPRESSA. MEDIOLANI, MDCCXXXIII. Apud Beniamin de
Sirturis, heredem Pacifici Pontii, & Piccaleae, Impressorem Archiepiscopalem, Cum
Privilegio.` Leaf n612 is a second setting of the same title with the same year,
and the terminal colophon at n598 carries the same imprint and year. THE FINDING
IS THEREFORE BIBLIOGRAPHIC AND NOT A RIGHTS DEFECT: 1733 is not 1961, and the
pre-1931 line reaches both strata with two centuries to spare. What the finding
changes is what the file may be called, which the edition record now says.

NOTHING LATER THAN 1733 IS IN THE FILE. A thirty-two-probe anachronism battery
over all 625 leaves found St Pius X absent, the Queenship absent, St Joseph the
Worker absent, Christ the King absent, St Therese absent, the Immaculate Heart
absent, `Signum magnum` and its dropped-initial form `ignum magnum` absent, the
1960 class ranks absent, the restored Holy Week absent, and no arabic year later
than 1712 anywhere except in worked examples inside the epact rubric. The probes
and their negatives are listed in
src/sources/inventories/ambrosian-and-mozarabic-rights-v1.toml.

THE SCAN AND ITS TEXT LAYER ADD NOTHING FOR ANYONE TO OWN. A faithful mechanical
reproduction of a public-domain work is not original authorship (Bridgeman Art
Library v. Corel Corp., 36 F. Supp. 2d 191 (S.D.N.Y. 1999)), and machine optical
character recognition adds no human authorship on top of it: this text layer was
produced autonomously by tesseract 5.3.0-6-g76ae, per the item's own `ocr` and
`ocr_parameters` fields, and there is no author to hold a right in it. Bridgeman's
limit -- it frees a scan of public-domain matter and says nothing about a scan of
anything else -- bites on nothing here, because both strata are free.

THE DIGITISING LIBRARY IS NOT THE UPLOADER, AND THAT IS A DIFFERENT RIGHTS SHAPE
FROM A BARE PUBLIC-DOMAIN MARK. The commissioning brief described this as a
Bayerische Staatsbibliothek item rather than an Internet Archive one. THE
CORRECTION IS SHARPER THAN THAT AND CUTS THE OTHER WAY: it is an Internet Archive
item, `10869665bsb`, uploaded on 24 May 2026 by a PRIVATE INDIVIDUAL
(`pavelserebrjanyi@gmail.com`) into the `german-online-libraries` collection, and
its `source_url` field points back to the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek's own
digitisation at https://www.digitale-sammlungen.de/en/view/bsb10869665. The scan
is BSB's -- the last leaf of the file, n624, is BSB's own digitisation card,
`Bayerische StaatsBibliothek / MDZ Munchener DigitalisierungsZentrum / Digitale
Bibliothek / Missale Ambrosianum / Mediolanum 1712 / Res/2 Liturg. 182 /
urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb10869665-9`. THE ITEM CARRIES NO `licenseurl` AND NO RIGHTS
FIELD AT ALL. So unlike the 1499 and the 1640 there is no host mark here even to
decline to rely on, and the basis rests entirely on the 1712 and 1733 imprints
and on Bridgeman. The MDZ's published practice is to serve public-domain
digitisations under the Public Domain Mark 1.0, which permits copying,
modification and distribution including for commercial purposes without
permission, and to state its rights position per object; the object page could
not be loaded from this run and IS THEREFORE NOT RELIED ON IN EITHER DIRECTION.
It could not enlarge or shrink the copyright status of books printed in 1712 and
1733 in any case. The rights record states the position for all three hosts met
in this lane.

NOT RELIED ON, EXPRESSLY: that the Internet Archive item is available, that the
download succeeded, or that the item carries no rights field.
guidance/sources.md:395-400 holds the first two insufficient for `tracked`, and
the third was never a basis in either direction -- the same discipline the Braga
record applied to the same absence.

ODESCALCHI Sanctae Mediolanensis Ecclesiae Archiepiscopi`, Benedetto Odescalchi-Erba, Archbishop of Milan 1712-1740. TWO ARCHBISHOPS, TWENTY-ONE YEARS APART, IN ONE VOLUME.

work.author: Archdiocese of Milan
work.description: The altar book of the Ambrosian rite -- the Latin use of the church of Milan, the largest non-Roman Latin rite still celebrated, and one of the uses left standing by the exempting clause of Quo primum. It is a Missal in the ordinary sense and it is NOT the Missale Romanum: it carries its own kalendar with its own Milanese archbishop-saints, its own Ordo Missae and Canon, a temporal cycle that begins six Sundays before Christmas, its own Holy Week and Easter Vigil, Commons, votive and Requiem Masses, blessings and Mass tones. IT MUST NOT BE FILED WITH THE ROMAN BOOK. work.catholic-church.missale-romanum is the Roman Rite's book; this is a different rite's, and the edge that does not exist between them is the point -- src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml records at its own line note that drawing one from the Roman line into the Ambrosian would assert a derivation in exactly the direction history runs the other way. It is registered under the archdiocese, on the pattern of work.archdiocese-of-braga.missale-bracarense, because the rite is the church of Milan's and the authority over the book has been the archbishop's throughout its printed tradition. The three editions registered here are printings, not promulgations: none of them carries a papal instrument, and what the 1640 and 1712 carry instead is an archbishop's own letter to his clergy.
